sentences.text:
This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.1797/2016 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Perumbavoor, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 06/07/2019.
The sole respondent herein is the second respondent/insurer in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 27/10/2016 at about 08:15 a.m., while she was travelling in bus bearing registration no.KL-17/A-6676 through the Ponjassery- Chithrapuzha road and when she reached the place by name Kizhakkambalam Ambalappady, lorry bearing registration No.KL- 17/B-9353 driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent 2025:KER:59120 MACA NO. 436 OF 2020 manner collided with the bus, as a result of which she sustained grievous injuries.
A sum of 25,00,000/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.
3. The first respondent/owner-cum driver remained ex parte.
4. The second respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the existence of a valid policy in respect of the offending vehicle, but denied negligence on the part of the first respondent.
It was contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the bus in which the claim petitioner was travelling.
5. Before the Tribunal, PW1 was examined and Exts.A1 to A20 and Ext.C1 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No documentary evidence was adduced by the second respondent/insurer.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and after hearing both sides,
found negligence on the part of the first respondent/owner-cum-driver of 2025:KER:59120 \ the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 13,69,117/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides 9.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner - Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the latter was working as staff nurse and was drawing an amount of 15,000/- as salary per month.
However, the Tribunal fixed the monthly income as 11,000/- despite production of Ext.A17 salary certificate and the testimony of the claim petitioner who was examined as PW1.
Therefore, the argument is that the 2025:KER:59120 MACA NO. 436 OF 2020 income needs to be refixed as per Ext.A17.
Per contra, it is submitted by the learned senior counsel appearing for the second respondent/insurer that the income fixed is reasonable and that it does not call for any interference by this Court.

2 9.1.
Going by Ext.A17 certificate, the claim petitioner was drawing a salary of 13,659/-.
PW1, when examined, stands by her case that she was getting an amount of 13,659/- per month.
That being the position, I find that the monthly income of the claim petitioner can be fixed as 13,700/-.
Percentage of permanent disability 10.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the functional disability fixed as 20% is quite low in the light of the injuries and disabilities sustained pursuant to the accident.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned senior counsel appearing for the second respondent/insurer that the percentage of disability fixed as 20% is correct in the light of the injuries and disabilities sustained and there is no infirmity calling for an 2025:KER:59120 \ interference by this Court.

10.1. The materials on record show that following injuries were sustained by the claim petitioner:
"1) type 3 open comminuted supracondylar- intercondylar femur fracture with bone loss right.

2) fracture 1,2,3 ribs right, minimal hemo- pneumothorax right, lung contusion."
10.2.
The claim petitioner was hospitalized for a total period of 36 days in four different spells.
She underwent four surgeries.

Ext.C1 certificate reads thus:
"Smt.Shiny Anil aged 45 years residing at Ovungamalil (H), Pulluvazhi P.O., whose medical board was constituted by Medical Superintendent of Government Medical College, Ernakulam, and a medical examination was done for her on 02/02/2018.
She entertains a diagnosis of United intercondylar supracondylar fracture (R) femur with knee stiffness, united fracture (R) 2,3,4 ribs.
She has a disability of 20% (Twenty percent).
1. The disability is classified as moderate.
2. This condition is likely to improve.

5. Recommend after a period of 1 year."
In the light of the injuries sustained and the resultant disabilities, I 2025:KER:59120 MACA NO.
436 OF 2020 find that the percentage of disability fixed at 20% by the Tribunal is reasonable and that it does not call for any interference.
Pain and suffering 11.
It is pointed out that though an amount of 10,00,000/- was claimed under this head, the Tribunal has granted an amount of 1,25,000/- only.

In the light of the injuries sustained; the period of hospitalization and the surgeries undergone by the claim petitioner, I find that an amount of 1,50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
